decisions.quote: To recalculate the ratio with the new controls, for the CFS data we used the frequencies provided by Perez et al. in their Table 1 .
decisions.reason: Rather than collecting a new sample of CFS patients, the authors re-analyzed the original study's published CFS allele frequencies from Table 1 of Perez et al. (2019) against alternative control reference datasets (openSNP 23andMe controls and NCBI ALFA). Under the codebook, re-analyzing the original study's own data under alternative control specifications is a reproduction, not a replication.

decisions.quote: The genetic predispositions reported for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome are not supported when reanalyzed with more appropriate control data including those drawn from the same 23andMe pool as the CFS patients. Out of the original 50 genomic positions presented to have the most prevalent deleterious polymorphisms among CFS sufferers, only three remained that met the original study criterion of at least twice as frequent as healthy individuals.
decisions.reason: Because the study is a reproduction, outcomes are coded on the two reproduction axes. Computational reproducibility of the original ratios was not checked (the authors took the reported CFS and Kaviar frequencies directly from Perez et al.'s Table 1 and went straight to recalculating ratios with alternative controls), and the robustness re-analysis overturned nearly all of the original top-50 genetic risk findings (only 3 of 50 SNPs remained above the 2.0 ratio threshold), establishing robustness challenges.
